title: openai-dispatch-adapter: stable tool_assignment format and streaming message framing
author: Anika Patel
description:
Motivation: OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling has several underspecified edge cases in our streaming path that cause fragmented tool invocation payloads to be rejected or mis-parsed by the backend. In practice this shows up as partial JSON objects in the streaming delta, inconsistent tool selection semantics (tool_choice vs ambiguous heuristics), and mismatches between caller schemas and our internal tool interface. This PR introduces a small adapter layer plus a stable streaming framing format to make tool invocation and tool responses deterministic across fragment boundaries and compatible with OpenAI-style calls.

Summary of changes: implement an OpenAI dispatch adapter that maps incoming OpenAI-style schemas to Redwood's internal tool interface (and vice‑versa). Introduce a first-class "tool_assignment" shape that replaces ad-hoc tool_choice semantics in the compatibility layer: it contains {tool, rationale, confidence_pct} and is emitted as a single, canonical event. Add message framing for streaming tool invocations: the runtime now emits discrete events: tool_response_start, tool_response_chunk, tool_response_end. Each chunk is boundary-safe (length-prefixed + base64 payload when necessary) to avoid broken JSON when clients receive partial frames. Include a compatibility shim: we will accept legacy tool_call payloads for a 90-day deprecation period and translate them into tool_assignment internally.

Why this design: making the selection explicit (tool_assignment) removes brittle heuristics from the streaming path, reduces ambiguity for downstream routing, and makes telemetry precise (we can attribute requests to a specific assigned tool even if the streaming content is incomplete). Framing tool_response_* events makes reassembly robust and isolates parsing logic to the adapter layer; this also slightly reduces CPU overhead in the reassembly path because we avoid repeated JSON parse errors.

Checklist:
- [x] dispatch adapter abstraction and serializer
- [x] streaming framing implementation and API contract
- [x] end-to-end tests (unit + integration + fuzz for fragmentation)
- [x] docs and compatibility notes in docs/openai-compatibility.md
- [x] updated SDK snippet for TypeScript and Python examples
- [ ] public changelog entry (follow-up with docs team)

Compatibility and migration notes: the adapter accepts both the new tool_assignment shape and the old tool_call/tool_choice variants. When an old payload is received we convert it to tool_assignment and emit a deprecation warning on the request-level headers (X-Redwood-Compat: tool_call-deprecated). Clients that rely on raw stream delta JSON should update to handle tool_response_* events; the SDKs were updated in this change to provide helpers that reassemble fragments and emit a single tool_response object to callers.

Performance: microbenchmarks show a ~3% median latency improvement for tool-heavy workloads due to reduced parse-retry cycles and simpler routing in the hot path. Memory overhead for the adapter is negligible (single-digit KBs) and the tests include a small canary run in perf-canary to validate tail latency.

Testing: added fuzz tests that fragment tool invocation JSON across random byte boundaries, integration tests that exercise legacy and new payloads, and an end-to-end demo script in examples/tool_assignment that demonstrates the framing and SDK reassembler. CI flakiness in streaming tests was addressed by adding deterministic chunking in tests and a retry harness for intermittent network simulation.

Docs: docs/openai-compatibility.md includes the new contract, examples for streaming, and migration guidance. The SDK examples in redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-sdk-python show how to use the new adapter and reassembler helpers.

Related: ENG-721 (design spec), ENG-789 (perf follow-up), SUP-4321 (customer case that surfaced partial stream failures)

merge_commit_message:
Squash: openai dispatch adapter + stable tool_assignment framing

Implements adapter, framing, tests, and docs (ENG-721, ENG-789)
release_notes: Stabilizes OpenAI-compatible tool assignment and streaming framing. Introduces an OpenAI dispatch adapter that maps OpenAI callable schemas to Redwood tools, adds robust streaming message framing for tool responses, and provides a 90-day compatibility shim for legacy payloads.
